catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class carries a per-channel linear stage position in micrometres. cap.motion.joint_position.v1 declares joint_positions in radians for every joint (the catalogue class output and units), while this controller's three channels are linear stages whose own position is in micrometres; cap.motion.cartesian_pose.v1 is restricted to robot.arm (this device is motion.axis) and carries no channel selection; cap.sensing.read.v1 is a sensor read, not a motion command. The extension keeps the native micrometre unit and lets the runtime enforce the operator's per-channel travel.

notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/labs/amsikking__thorlabs_mcm3000 --backend fake (exit 0; G1-G3 and G5-G9 pass and G4 carries only the expected REF_BINARY warning; evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). The only finding is the expected G4.REF_BINARY warning for the vendor PDF citation of the Stop Command; check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the package is a direct Driver with a native.py factory, not the card's family-config/SerialDriver helper. The upstream builds framed binary commands at run time (0A 04 <channel> 00 00 00 for a position query, 53 04 06 00 00 00 <channel word> <count> for a move, thorlabs_MCM3000.py:97-102 and 135-138); a command table cannot reproduce those bytes, and changing their syntax to pass G7 would be wrong. NOT COVERED: the private encoder-zeroing routine, the private non-blocking _finish_move path, the configurable encoder tolerance, very_verbose logging, and the controller's motor-status query (the upstream docstring says it is not working); only the three channel positions, one channel move, the stop and the e-stop are exposed. There are no writable state fields, so cap.device.configure.v1 has no parameters. No cap.motion.home.v1 is exposed because the upstream has no home command: its example homes by an absolute move to 0 um. LIMITS: position_um is Limit.operator_required because the travel follows the stage entry chosen in the constructor stages argument; the clone's table gives ZFM2020/ZFM2030 +/-12700 um and MMP-2XY +/-25400 um (thorlabs_MCM3000.py:42-44) and _legalize_move_um refuses outside the selected entry (167-170), so one static bound would be a guess for the connected stage. Every move is refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET until the operator's site-limits.json supplies it; site-limits.example.json is an example for one bench (+/-100 um), not a statement about any unit. The channel input is bounded to 0, 1, 2 by the three-entry constructor and the channels built from non-None stage entries (thorlabs_MCM3000.py:32-54). STOP: the upstream class implements no stop method (docstring lines 7-8). The stop and e-stop send the vendor protocol's abrupt Stop Command 65 04 <channel> 01 00 00 to every configured channel through the upstream's own _send frame writer (MCM3000_Direct_Serial_Communication.pdf:2). That page cannot be checked by the gate (G4.REF_BINARY); the page was read for this package and a reviewer should open page 2 of that 4-page document. No text file of the clone states the stop command, and no independent hardware e-stop is documented, so none is claimed. FAKE: package-local in-memory stand-in, not a recording; it answers the query, move, set-zero and stop frames, moves instantly, ignores reverse and encoder quantisation and models no timing, timeout or controller fault. Its conversion factors and starting positions are marked placeholders, not facts. HARDWARE: never attached; native.py and the upstream package were never imported or executed and no hardware run is claimed. The package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by null). It is R1, so the loader's refusal of a model-written hardware backend applies only at R2 and R3; the hardware backend remains an operator decision and no protection beyond the SDK and the controller's stop command is claimed.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-10-30; reviewed_by stays null): not accepted by a model, so a human signature is still needed: the e-stop sends the vendor Stop Command, which only the PDF MCM3000_Direct_Serial_Communication.pdf states (page 2; the upstream class has no stop), and the Fact citing that page is an UNVERIFIABLE_CITATION. The reviewer opened the page's figure (header only: 65 04, Chan Ident, Stop Mode, 00 00) and found the frame the driver sends matches it; the meaning of stop mode 0x01 is in the page's text, which the reviewer could not read. A human opens page 2 and signs reviewed_by; until then collect.py --strict warns. The DEVIATION FROM THE CARD is accepted: a registry override now makes the card a direct driver. After the registry rebuild refreshed task.json, the reviewer re-ran the gate and wrote its digest above.

MODEL REVIEW (gpt-6-astra, a model and not a human, 2026-11-06; reviewed_by stays null): Citation check requested by the owner (Codex gpt-6-astra, reasoning effort max): page 2 of MCM3000_Direct_Serial_Communication.pdf (vector outlines, so the page was rendered with macOS PDFKit and transcribed) reads 'Stop Command. This command stops any type of motor move on the specified channel. Command structure (6 bytes): 65 04 Chan Ident Stop Mode 00 00 ... Stop Mode: This device has only one Stop Mode (abrupt). Set this byte to 0x01.' Every part of the fact matches. The PDF calls the Stop Mode format 'word' while its diagram gives one byte; that does not contradict the fact. A model check is not a signature: collect still lists the citation for a human reviewer.
